_note: SSA Benefit Formula Bend Points (PIA formula) AND Quarter-of-Coverage (QC) earnings thresholds, Social Security Administration Office of the Chief Actuary. Bend points source: https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/bendpoints.html (retrieved 2026-08-31). QC threshold source: https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/QC.html (retrieved 2026-08-31, historical table 1978-2026 -- 1978 itself, $250/QC, is not included here since this file starts at 1979 to match the bend points table's own range). Bend points keyed by YEAR OF ELIGIBILITY (age 62/disability/death); qc_threshold is the earnings needed for one quarter of coverage (credit) in that SAME calendar year, capped at 4 credits/year no matter how high earnings are -- modules/social_security.py applies the CURRENT (or eligibility-year) qc_threshold flat across every year of a real earnings record (does not look up each historical year's own threshold), the same documented simplification already used for the SS wage base (2026-08-30). All dollar amounts are monthly (bend points) or annual (qc_threshold), nominal for their own year -- both held flat in real terms for any year beyond the last one configured, same convention as modules/tax.py's own bracket tables. 2026-09-06 addition: 'earnings_test_lower_exempt'/'earnings_test_higher_exempt' (Retirement Earnings Test annual exempt amounts, https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2026.html and https://www.ssa.gov/benefits/retirement/planner/whileworking.html, both retrieved 2026-09-06) -- lower applies to every year strictly BEFORE the one Full Retirement Age is reached in ($1 withheld per $2 earned above it), higher applies only to the FRA year itself, only to earnings before the month FRA is reached ($1 withheld per $3 earned above it; this table has no sub-annual precision, so modules/social_security.py applies it to the full FRA year -- a documented, flagged approximation, see that module's own docstring). **A REAL, IMPORTANT SEMANTIC DIFFERENCE from bend_point_1/bend_point_2/qc_threshold above: these two new fields are keyed by the CALENDAR YEAR being evaluated, not year of eligibility** -- modules/social_security.py's earnings_test_exempt_amounts_for_year looks them up by the literal projected year directly, never by ssa_effective_birth_year(...)+62 the way bend_points_for_year/qc_threshold_for_year do; only added starting 2026 (the year this feature shipped) since a real caller only ever evaluates a current-or-future year, never before.
